notes:
Short summary: Penumbra is a digital-first financial services provider building an omnichannel banking assistant + reconciliation/reranking pipelines. They're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation (VPC/on-prem option). Primary ask: a sizing workshop that converts their telemetry into a concrete reserved GPU plan + latency SLO guarantees they can put in an SLA. Key quantitative inputs they provided: baseline QPS ~120 (steady-state business hours), typical request size 40–90 tokens (avg ~58), synchronous chat paths require p95 < 180ms and p99 < 400ms, heavy reranking jobs run asynchronously at batch sizes ~128 embeddings but need sub-second tail for top-k. Peak events (promo/statement runs) show 3–4x spike to ~420 QPS sustained for ~20 minutes; monthly batch reconciliation windows produce long-running token/sec-intensive workloads (streaming >200k tokens/min).

Workshop goals (customer expectations):
- Map baseline QPS and tokens/sec to GPU vCPU/IO requirements and recommend instance family (H100 vs A100 vs LLM-optimized accelerator).
- Produce reserve sizing with headroom for 2x burst and explicit autoscale+burst policy; specify expected tokens/sec per-GPU for their model family and quantization profile.
- Deliver candidate SLA language: throughput guarantee tiers (committed, burst), latency SLOs (p95/p99), and failure/fallback behavior (model downgrade -> hosted variant).
- Provide cost model showing committed vs on-demand delta and suggested commit size to meet their ARR target.

Technical notes from SE session (Luis):
- Candidate model family: open-llm-3b / 7b variants; recommend 4-bit quantized runtime for embeddings and 8-bit path for chat generation unless higher fidelity required.
- Measured tokens/sec per A100-80GB (quant-4): 8k–10k tokens/sec for generation pipeline with batching; H100 shows 1.6–2x uplift in low-latency single-stream scenarios.
- Suggested reserved capacity: baseline -> 3x A100-80GB equivalent (to cover 120 QPS at avg 58 tokens with 40ms batching window); peak headroom plan: add 6 additional GPUs for 3x spike with short-burst autoscale.
- Caching: recommend prefix/KV-cache for common prompts to reduce effective tokens/sec by estimated 12–18% on conversational traffic.

POC / Workshop deliverables expected:
1) Sizing workbook (spreadsheet) translating their QPS/tokens to GPU counts by latency SLO and model choice.
2) SLA / pricing draft with committed vs burst tiers + rollback policy.
3) Short runbook for migration to Private VPC (network egress, IP allowlist, KMS integration checklist).
4) Perf test plan + acceptance criteria for go/no-go.
